title: Open redirect in safeNext(): a backslash path ('/\evil.com') passes the '//' check and new URL() resolves it to an external host; flows through sl_oauth into /api/auth/callback's post-login redirect
steps: Pass next='/\evil.com' (a single leading slash then a backslash): it is accepted unchanged.
The login route stores next in the signed sl_oauth cookie; /api/auth/callback then does NextResponse.redirect(new URL(dest, req.url)) with dest=next on a successful Whop login.
new URL('/\evil.com', 'http://host') === 'http://evil.com/' because WHATWG URL normalises '\' to '/', making it protocol-relative -> external redirect.
expected: safeNext should only ever return a same-origin path; backslashes / control chars that URL parsers fold into '//' must be rejected (or the path re-validated after new URL() against the app origin).
actual: '/\evil.com' is treated as a safe local path and redirects off-site to evil.com after a completed OAuth login. Verified: new URL('/\evil.com', base) -> http://evil.com/. Not reproducible end-to-end on QA because WHOP_CLIENT_ID is unset (/api/auth/login -> /login?error=not_configured); reachable on a Whop-configured production deployment.
suspected_area: app/src/lib/whop.ts safeNext — insufficient allowlist; also /api/auth/callback re-redirects to next without re-checking origin.
